predecessors.name: Edessa Under Thoros
predecessors.text: Edessa itself, from which Thoros was removed in March 1098

predecessors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
predecessors.text: the rest of the county (Turbessel, Ravendan and the Euphrates towns) that Baldwin seized in early 1098

successors.name: Zengid dynasty
successors.text: Edessa (24 December 1144) and Saruj (January 1145) to Zengi, then Turbessel in 1151 to 'Nur ad-Din's captain Hassan'

successors.name: Byzantine Empire
successors.text: Turbessel and the rest of the county, 'sold ... to Manuel I Comnenus' in 1150

successors.name: Sultanate of Rum
successors.text: the county 'mostly absorbed by Mesud, Timurtash of Mardin, and Nur ad-Din' in 1150-1151

successors.name: Artuqids
successors.text: the share of Timurtash of Mardin, unlocated on the page

rulers.name: Tancred (regent for the captive Baldwin II)
rulers.title: regent

ledger.x: 1098: Baldwin of Boulogne founds the County of Edessa, the first crusader state.
1100: Baldwin of Boulogne leaves for Jerusalem and Baldwin of Bourcq becomes count.

ledger.cp: Jikirmish of Mosul and Sokman of Mardin

ledger.x: 7 May 1104: Baldwin and Joscelin are captured at Harran.
ledger.cp: Jikirmish of Mosul and Sokman of Mardin

ledger.x: Page silent: Cliopatria's 1111 shape adds a strip north to 38.4 N (Kesoun, Raban, Behesni, Hisn Mansur).

ledger.cp: Vasil Dgha (Armenian lord of Kesoun and Raban)

ledger.x: 1117: Birecik surrenders after a siege of about a year.
Page silent: no page opened dates an acquisition near 1126; the county article gives none before 1144.
1144: the count's seat moves from Edessa to Turbessel.
27 October 1146: Joscelin II breaks into Edessa.
November 1146: Nur ad-Din drives Joscelin out of Edessa after the battle of 3 November.
1150: Joscelin II's wife sells Turbessel and the rest of the county to Manuel I.
1151: the last of the county falls.

wars.name: Battle of Harran
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory on 7 May 1104: Baldwin II and Joscelin were captured; Tancred became regent of Antioch and of Edessa.

wars.name: Mosul and Artuqid attacks on Edessa
wars.outcome: Sokman attacked Saruj in early 1101; Mawdud besieged Edessa in April 1110 and April-June 1112 and Turbessel in July 1111; Aqsunqur invaded in May 1114.

wars.name: Siege of Edessa (1144)
wars.outcome: Zengi besieged Edessa from 28 November 1144, entered on 24 December and took the citadel on 26 December; he took Saruj in January 1145.

wars.name: Siege of Edessa (1146)
wars.outcome: Joscelin II retook the city but not the citadel on 27 October; Nur ad-Din drove him out in November.

wars.name: Conquest of the county by Nur ad-Din and Mas'ud
wars.outcome: Nur ad-Din captured Joscelin II in 1150; Turbessel and the rest were sold to Manuel I, then fell in 1151 to Nur ad-Din's captain Hassan, Mesud and Timurtash of Mardin.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines are given by any page; the county was a chain of towns and fortresses (Edessa, Saruj, Samosata, Turbessel, Birecik) whose outline is approximate throughout.
